title: Why is the sky blue at noon and red at sunset?

cards.title: It's the same sky and the same Sun.
cards.text: The Sun looks yellow, but its light is really all colours mixed together. Air looks clear, but it isn't quite.
cards.hook: So how does clear air turn sunlight into a blue sky, and later a red and orange sunset?

notes: The Sun looks yellow, but its light is all colours mixed
How does clear air turn it into a blue sky, and later a red and orange sunset?

cards.title: Air is made of molecules that scatter light in all directions
cards.text: Light travels in waves, and each colour has its own length. Blue waves are short and red waves are long. Air is made of molecules, tiny bits of gas far too small to see. They scatter light, which means they send it off in all directions.
cards.hook: So does air scatter blue light the same as red light?

notes: Light travels in waves, and each colour has its own length
Air is made of molecules, tiny bits of gas far too small to see
They scatter light: they send it off in all directions

cards.title: Air scatters blue about four times as strongly as red, so the blue comes from all over the sky
cards.text: Air scatters blue about four times as strongly as red, so far more blue than red is sent off. That scattered blue reaches your eyes from all over the sky. The sky has no blue of its own. The blue was in the sunlight all along.
cards.hook: So why is a sunset red and orange?

notes: Air scatters blue about four times as strongly as red
That scattered blue reaches your eyes from all over the sky

cards.title: At sunset the Sun's light slants through far more air, so red and orange are what is left
cards.text: At sunset the Sun is low, so its light slants through far more air. Right at the horizon, that is about 38 times as much air as when the Sun is straight overhead. On the way, much of the blue is scattered off in other directions and never reaches you. Red and orange are what is left. The Sun looks yellow at noon for the same reason. The air has already scattered some blue out of its light.
cards.takeaway: The same scattering that makes the sky blue takes much of the blue out of the sunset.

notes: Sun overhead: a short path through the air
At sunset the Sun is low, so its light slants through far more air
Much of the blue is scattered off in other directions
Red and orange are what is left

cards.note: Clouds are white because their drops of water are much bigger than air molecules, and they scatter all the colours alike.
